tagline: Argentina's Alpine-style Patagonian resort town pairs a mountain lake as blue as Switzerland with the country's best chocolate, ski slopes and the famous Seven Lakes road.
overview: San Carlos de Bariloche sits on the shore of Nahuel Huapi, a glacial lake ringed by snowy Andes peaks. Founded in 1902 and settled by Swiss, German and Austrian immigrants, its log-and-stone architecture and chocolate shops earned it the nickname 'Little Switzerland'.

The town is Argentina's mountain playground. In winter, Cerro Catedral — South America's biggest ski resort — fills with skiers; in summer, kayaks and sailboats take to the lake and hikers ride chairlifts to views over the national park. The Circuito Chico drive curves past viewpoints, breweries and the Llao Llao hotel.

Everything here comes with chocolate: Bariloche has been Argentina's chocolate capital since Italian immigrants opened shops in the 1940s. Day trips follow the Seven Lakes route north to San Martín de los Andes or south to El Bolsón's hippy market.

funFacts.title: LITTLE SWITZERLAND
funFacts.text: Alpine architecture, chocolate shops and snowy peaks earned Bariloche its Swiss nickname.

funFacts.title: ARGENTINA'S CHOCOLATE CAPITAL
funFacts.text: Italian immigrants founded the chocolate industry in the 1940s — shops line Mitre street.

funFacts.title: SOUTH AMERICA'S BIGGEST SKI RESORT
funFacts.text: Cerro Catedral offers around 120 kilometres of pistes with views over the lake.

funFacts.title: THE SEVEN LAKES
funFacts.text: The scenic Ruta de los Siete Lagos links seven glacial lakes through the forest.

funFacts.title: A PARK FOUNDED IN 1934
funFacts.text: Nahuel Huapi was Argentina's first national park, modelled on Yellowstone.

funFacts.title: A LEGENDARY HOTEL
funFacts.text: The Llao Llao hotel, rebuilt after a 1938 fire, is an icon of Patagonian architecture.

funFacts.title: CERRO TRONADOR
funFacts.text: The 'Thunderer' glacier volcano nearby is named for the sound of its ice avalanches.

funFacts.title: A HITLER MYTH
funFacts.text: Wild conspiracy theories claimed Nazi fugitives hid here — historians debunk most, but the myth persists.

funFacts.title: SMOKED FISH & CURANTO
funFacts.text: Mapuche curanto feasts and smoked trout are the regional table.

funFacts.title: CROSSING TO CHILE
funFacts.text: The Andean Lakes Crossing connects Bariloche to Puerto Varas by boats and buses.
